verdict.pair_reasons:
X vs Y — tie. Both are accurate on the gate's mechanics and neither fabricates a citation; their specific verified advantages cut in opposite directions and roughly balance. X uniquely catches two things the key names: the quoted-model bypass (`--model "fable"` cannot match the class `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` at :75, so the fire is uncounted — M5), which is a genuine omission from Y's "every shape that makes the gate not count" table, and the stale citation inside the enforcer itself (gate:27 → scripts/handoff-fire.sh:9303-9311, which is hf_inflight_key at :9304-9318 — M8), which Y's stated audit scope structurally excluded. X also uniquely flags skills/frontier-run/SKILL.md:30 ("reads only active + end") as false against :40/:114/:120/:125, and names the exact M10 instance (frontier-routing SKILL.md:40-42). Y, conversely, audited far more citations and verified five stale/wrong ones X never opened (p15-escalation.md:44, A5-harness.md:357, A6-mechanics.md:245 and :500, and L1-census.md:62, which is wrong rather than stale — :138 says `--model opus` and tests/frontier-spawn-gate.bats:155 forbids `--model claude-opus-`), and Y alone found config/hook-chains.d/pretooluse-bash:7-8,:18-27, a second independently maintained roster of ten PreToolUse Bash hooks that also omits the gate — real corroboration for item 7. X carries four minor off-by-one citation slips (fallback cited at :700 not :699; the no-refund phrase at :689-690 not :690-691); Y carries three of comparable weight (a miscounted CC_LADDER grep, grep hits attributed to :134/:144). Both miss K19 and M6.

X vs Z — Z. Z states everything X does on the enforcer and adds, all verified against the snapshot: K19 (scripts/handoff-fire.sh:9493 resolves the fable alias from the same SSOT key the gate reads — X never cites it); M6 (TMPDIR and the unprotected counter file as a reset lever); the five stale doc citations X skipped; and four material findings X lacks — that migrations/0029:39-40's "fails OPEN … missing/unreadable SSOT" is false on the unreadable half (confirmed: `[ -f ]` at :37 passes, `active` is empty, :117 fails, the gate exits 2), that install.sh:29/:1203-1204/:1216-1218 explains why an install never registers the Bash arm, that 0029's own verify/conflict oracles (:6-7) read one of the five dirs it writes, and that agent-teams-enforce.sh:366-367's "attempts are charged, not admissions" is the opposite of the gate it cites (verified by reading both: agent-teams-enforce increments at :423-424 before refusing at :438; the gate checks at :136 and increments at :144). Z's citations are also more precise where X drifts (:690-691, :699, :9304-9318). X's only advantages are the frontier-run SKILL.md:30 catch and the exact frontier-routing SKILL.md:41 instance of M10 — outweighed several times over.

Y vs Z — Z. Z hits four key items Y misses outright (K19, M5, M6, M8) plus the launcher-name trap (:25-32) and the prefix-vs-equality consequence tied to test 5 and mutant 21 (:89, :223), and covers the same doc-citation audit Y does (p15:44, A5:357, A6:245/:500, L1-census:62, model-config:545, agent-teams-enforce:366) while adding L1-census:61 and model-config:937. Z also corrects the reachability claim Y overstates: Y says the closed-window branch is unreachable "unless `active` is manually flipped", while Z shows a present-but-broken SSOT reaches it — the key's K2 precision note confirms Z. Y's real unique win is the hook-chains.d corroboration; Z substitutes an equally material and equally verified angle (install.sh's additive-merge semantics) and carries only one trivial citation slip against Y's three.
